10	
11	In the RCT2 coaster contest (rounds started 2026-07-27), the reported `score` equals the ride's
12	`excitement` after a stock-similarity penalty. Measurements from round 2 (steel twister, ride_type 51):
13	
14	- **Hard cliff at intensity 10.0.** Same 99-piece layout: I=8.42 → E=6.85; I=10.58 → E=5.14;
15	  an early sloppy build at I=14.30 → E=1.97. Excitement is multiplied down in steps once
16	  intensity crosses 10, so *target intensity 8–9.5 and never above 10*.
17	- **Mid-course brakes are nearly free excitement.** Inserting two `{"t":"brakes","speed":18}`
18	  before the first corkscrew dropped intensity 10.22 → 7.63 with excitement *unchanged* at 6.74.
19	  Max lateral G fell 3.03 → 2.38, max positive G 4.83 → 4.09. High-speed corkscrews were the
20	  lateral-G source, not the banked turns.
21	- **Spend the headroom on lift height.** With intensity bought down, raising the chain lift
22	  (18 → 22 `up_25`) and adding a 4th `down_60` took highest_drop 28 → 36 and E 6.74 → 6.85.
23	- Inversions are worth roughly +0.1 E each (4 → 5 gave 6.63 → 6.74); airtime hills gave
24	  ~+0.16 E for +0.21 intensity. Both are weaker levers than drop height.
25	
26	Round 3 (best 6.99, I=8.45) added two more measurements:
27	
28	- **The brake-clamp trick works.** Put a `brakes` at the bottom of the first drop and the whole
29	  downstream layout runs at *identical* speeds no matter how tall the lift is. That decouples
30	  `highest_drop`/`max_speed` (which score) from the G-forces of everything after (which cost
31	  intensity). Lift 29→33 `up_25` + 5→6 `down_60` took highest_drop 52→60 with intensity
32	  unchanged at 8.45.
33	- **Excitement saturates around 7.** Going drop 36→52→60, drops 9→11, airtime 65→91, length
34	  672→839 moved E only 6.85→6.97→6.99. Past ~6.9 these levers return ~+0.02 each; don't burn a
35	  round chasing them.
36	- **Back-to-back corkscrews are an intensity bomb.** Swapping one flat hill for a 4-piece
37	  corkscrew chain (`right_up,left_down,left_up,right_down`, net 6·forward, dz 0 — a drop-in
38	  replacement for a 6-tile straight) took inversions 5→7 but intensity 8.45→**16.44** and
39	  excitement 6.97→**1.63**. Inversions must be spread out, never chained.
40	
41	Round 4 (best **7.04**, I=8.62) found the lever that beats the ~7 saturation:
42	
43	- **Average speed is the live lever, not drop height.** `average_speed` feeds excitement directly.
44	  Loosening the mid-course brakes (18→21 and 13→17) on the *identical* round-3 layout took
45	  average_speed 455354→470322 and E 6.99→**7.04** for only +0.17 intensity (8.45→8.62).
46	  The 34-piece chain lift is slow and eats most of `ride_time`, which is why average speed is low.
47	- **The intensity cliff is violently non-linear — step brakes by 1, never 3.** From the 7.04 config
48	  (first/tail/end brakes = 25/21/17): 25/23/19 → I=**10.76**, E=5.27. 28/24/20 → I=**15.97**, E=**1.62**.
49	  A +2 brake step cost 2.1 intensity; +3 cost 7.4. Bracket the optimum in steps of 1.
50	- **Brake `speed` quantizes — adjacent values are not distinct.** Tail brakes at (22,18) returned
51	  results *byte-identical* to (23,19): I=10.76, E=5.27, average_speed=482714. So the usable settings
52	  are coarser than 1 unit; 21/17 (I=8.62) and 22/18 (I=10.76) are ADJACENT rungs with nothing
53	  between them. Don't burn builds probing intermediate brake values — there is no fine tuning here,
54	  and on this layout 7.04 was provably the top rung under the cliff.
55	- **Two different brakes, two different failure modes.** The *first* brake (bottom of the big drop)
56	  sets vertical-loop entry speed → drives `max_positive_g`; leave it at 25. The *tail* brakes drive
57	  `max_lateral_g` in the final banked turns (2.55 at I=8.62 → 2.94 at I=10.76 with positive G
58	  unchanged at 4.70). Lateral G is what breaks the tail.
59	- **Corkscrew pairs are (+3, ∓3, 0), not (+3, 0, 0).** At dir 2, `right_corkscrew_up` is
60	  (+1,−2,+80,→dir3) and `left_corkscrew_down` from dir 3 is (+2,−1,−80,→dir2). So a pair shifts
61	  3 tiles *sideways* and can NOT be dropped into a straight run to add a cheap inversion.
62	
63	Round 5 (best **7.04** — could not beat round 4; five variants tested) mapped the drop/speed frontier.
64	All variants kept the round-4 layout after the first brake and changed only the lift and the tail:
65	
66	- **Boosters are the cheapest average-speed lever there is.** Replacing the tail's slow flats with
67	  `{"t":"booster","speed":30}` took average_speed 568177→597584 and max_speed back to ~68 mph
68	  (1.97M) for **+0.23 intensity**. Boosters on straight flat generate essentially no G. Always
69	  booster the straight run-in rather than coasting it.
70	- **Shortening the chain lift is a real but losing trade.** 33→13 `up_25` cut ride_time 89→68 and
71	  raised average_speed 470322→601221 (+28%), but highest_drop fell 60→20 and E fell 7.04→6.88.
72	  Roughly: +1% average speed ≈ +0.009 E, and drop 20→60 ≈ +0.35 E. The tall lift wins.
73	- **There is no middle ground — the cliff moves with the tail brakes.** With tail brakes at 22/18,
74	  BOTH drop 30 (lift 18) and drop 40 (lift 23) returned intensity **10.56** exactly and E≈5.3.
75	  `max_lateral_g` hit 2.87–2.92 (vs 2.55 at the 7.04 config). A taller drop feeds the back half
76	  faster, so lateral G in the closing banked turns — not positive G — is what trips the cliff.
77	  Raising drop height REQUIRES dropping tail brakes back to 21/17 in the same build.
78	- **Airtime hills in the run-in are not worth it.** Three bunny hops replacing flats took
79	  total_air_time 102→131 and num_drops 11→14, but intensity 7.89→8.55 and E 7.00→**6.95**.
80	  Contradicts the round-2 note that airtime hills pay; at booster speed on flat ground they don't.
81	- **Intensity quantizes hard at 10.56.** Two different layouts returned byte-identical
82	  intensity/nausea (10.56/6.13). Same coarse-rung behaviour as the brake speeds.
83	
84	**Why:** the whole game is maximising excitement *subject to* staying under the intensity cliff,
85	so the winning move order is: cut G-forces first, then re-spend the budget on drop height.
86	
87	**How to apply:** build a closed circuit and `finish_and_test` early to bank a score, then iterate
88	brakes-then-height. See [[rct2-coaster-circuit-closure]] for the geometry arithmetic.
89

2	name: rct2-coaster-circuit-closure
3	description: Geometry arithmetic for closing an RCT2 coaster circuit on paper before placing pieces
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 2e22e2bc-f0c5-4828-b26f-60e933cdc7da

9	---
10	
11	Closing the loop in the RCT2 coaster contest is pure bookkeeping; doing it on paper first meant
12	a 92-piece circuit closed on the very first `place_pieces` run with zero rejections.
13	
14	Directions: 0=-x, 1=+y, 2=+x, 3=-y. Left turn cycles 2→1→0→3→2; right turn is the reverse.
15	`piece_geometry` only reports deltas for one facing — rotate them yourself as
16	(forward, left) offsets rather than re-querying per turn.
17	
18	Key facts:
19	- **Height parity.** Any flat-to-flat sequence of 25°/60° pieces moves z by a multiple of 16, so
20	  every flat run sits at `station_z + 16k`. `half_loop_up` + `half_loop_down` is the exception: it
21	  enters flat and exits at down-25, netting **−8** after the levelling `down_25_to_flat`. That breaks
22	  parity and makes the station unreachable — pair it with a second half-loop combo, or skip half
23	  loops entirely (vertical loops and corkscrew pairs are both dz-neutral and parity-safe).
24	- **180° U-turn Δy budget.** From dir 0, two `banked_*_turn_5` give Δ(+1, ±5); turn_5 then turn_3
25	  gives Δ(0, ±4); two turn_3 give Δ(+1, ±3). Only 3/4/5 are reachable, so pick the return-leg y to
26	  match, or trim with `s_bend` (±1 in y, 3 tiles in x, at dir 0).
27	- Banked turns need `flat_to_*_bank` in and `*_bank_to_flat` out.
28	- The circuit closes when the cursor returns to the exact start x/y/z/dir/bank — the final piece
29	  *lands on* the `begin_station` tile, so approach it from one tile behind, facing the station.
30	
31	- **Ground level is z=112 and "Raise or lower land first" means the piece went under it.** The map
32	  is flat at 112 over the whole build area, so the deepest point of the layout, not the station,
33	  sets the required lift height. The round-4/5 layout descends **64 below its first brake**, so that
34	  brake must sit at z=176 — never 112. Check the deepest relative point before choosing the lift.
35	- **Re-deriving a piece count from a past eval report is the main source of wasted cycles.** Two
36	  separate rebuilds this round failed because a `down_60`/`up_25` run was miscounted by one or two.
37	  Count the run in the report explicitly, then verify the cursor z after the lift before continuing.
38	- **Changing the lift length shifts the whole layout in x.** Keep the post-brake section on identical
39	  terrain by solving for the station x: `station_x = 78 - (n_up_25) - (n_descent_pieces)` puts the
40	  first brake at x=85 as in the 7.04 build. The return leg always ends at x=34 regardless, so pad
41	  the run-in with `station_x - 34` extra tiles (boosters, not flats).
42	
43	**Why:** `place_pieces` stops at the first rejection, so a mis-planned return leg wastes a whole
44	build cycle out of a ~30-minute round.
45	
46	**How to apply:** trace absolute (x, y, z, dir) per piece before calling `place_pieces`, and pick
47	the station tile last so its y satisfies the U-turn Δy. See [[rct2-coaster-scoring-levers]].
48

text:
Round complete. Final score banked: **7.23**.

**What happened:** My first move was replaying the archived 7.04 layout to bank a floor, but my hand-transcribed lift run came out 16 height units short and hit "Raise or lower land first." Rather than re-derive it, I swapped the tail's final drop for flats — which scored **7.09**, beating the "correct" original. From there the real gain came from inversions: intensity was only 8.66 against the 10.0 cliff, so I spent that headroom on corkscrew pairs, each preceded by a brake to keep G-forces flat.

| Build | Inversions | Intensity | Excitement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repaired replay | 5 | 8.66 | 7.09 |
| +1 pair | 6 | 9.03 | **7.20** |
| +2 more | 7 | 9.52 | **7.23** |

Two things worth flagging: the last inversion pair only returned +0.03 for +0.49 intensity, so the trade goes bad around I≈9 — well before the cliff actually bites. And my final experiment (boosters 20→28) returned *byte-identical* excitement, intensity, nausea and G-forces despite moving average speed — small speed tweaks are below the rating's resolution, which corrects an over-broad note I'd written in round 4. I've updated both memory files, including the lateral-cancelling corkscrew trick ((left_up,right_down) + hill + (right_up,left_down) = a 10-tile straight worth +2 inversions with no drift) and the two-equation tail solver, which closed a 24-piece return leg first try twice.

**Sevenfold** — 139-piece steel twister, 60ft drop, 7 inversions (2 vertical loops + 5 corkscrew pairs), excitement **7.23** at intensity 9.52, styled bright red on black.
